stops.note: from a root meaning 'to see', denoting vision or sight
narrowed to mean the auspicious viewing of a deity or holy person
stops.meaning: the auspicious viewing of a deity or holy person

stops.note: adopted in English writing on Hindu religious practice
stops.meaning: the beholding of a deity, revered person, or sacred object

current_meaning: In Hindu practice, the auspicious act of seeing and being seen by a deity, revered teacher, or sacred image.
